title: Common quotient reduction of the geometric scalar comparison
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism of small-site topoi, with $u^{-1}$ left exact and left adjoint to $u_*$. Let $R\to B$ and $R'\to B'$ be flat morphisms of commutative ring sheaves. Give an identification $u^{-1}R\cong R'$ and a compatible map $u^{-1}B\to B'$. Let $J_n\subset R$ and $J_n'\subset R'$ be decreasing ideal sheaves such that the latter is generated by the image of $u^{-1}J_n$. Assume the induced maps identify $S_n=R/J_n=B/J_nB$ and $S_n'=R'/J_n'=B'/J_n'B'$, compatibly with transitions. In the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use K-flat ringed pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $M\in D(B)$ the scalar-insertion comparison
$$Lu_R^*\operatorname{Res}M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}'Lu_B^*M$$
has an invertible finite reduction. Its inverse is the canonical $S_n'$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}'Lu_B^*M\otimes_{R'}^L S_n'\cong Lu_R^*(\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n).$$
For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, insertion is induced by $r'\otimes p\mapsto\bar r'\otimes p$ from $R'\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}P$ to $\operatorname{Res}'(B'\otimes_{u^{-1}B}u^{-1}P)$, where $\bar r'$ is the image of $r'$ under $R'\to B'$ (so $1\otimes p\mapsto1\otimes p$). The isomorphisms are natural in $M$, compatible with quotient transitions and quotient units, and coherent for identity and composable geometric morphisms with such data under the canonical pullback compositors. Tensor and pure sections are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]; K-flatness and flatness are [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

proof.text: Construct the ordinary insertion using restrictionIso, the normalized scalar-extension adjunction unit and restrictionComp. Its section formula is precisely insertion of 1. Assemble its homotopy computation square as a natural transformation; the target computation is invertible on flat-term K-flat objects. Descend by fully faithful whiskering along their localization, obtaining Insertion with the specified representative equation.

Every quotient reduction of this insertion is invertible by the finite insertion theorem. Take asIso for the finite comparison, and define its inverse by composing its inverse with the given coefficient tensor comparison.

The unit equation is naturality of the quotient-extension adjunction unit. Package reductionTransition as a natural transformation using the second unit and normalized scalar-extension and restriction compositors; its naturality gives the transition equation.

Composition normalization of unreduced insertion gives the first composition law. Applying quotient scalar extension, preserving composition, gives its finite equation. Identity normalization gives the unreduced identity law; again scalar extension gives the finite identity.

proof_origin.note: Actual Lean construction from normalized scalar adjunction units and flat-term K-flat localization. Unit and transition equations are naturality; finite coherence is scalar extension of unreduced coherence.

The item statement is true. On a flat-term K-flat P, both finite reductions equal u^{-1}P/J_n'. This holds because A/J_n'A = u^{-1}(B/J_nB) = u^{-1}(R/J_n) = S_n', and the unreduced map is never claimed invertible. Small cases checked: J_n=R; u=id; R=B; J_n=0. The delivery has no new nodes, and the item's statement and stmt_deps are unchanged against live. There is no cycle; the only citer is lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence, at step 4. The item is not dropped, has no repair note, and is still unsplit on live. Stacks tag/label pairs checked: 06YY, 0G7E, 06YS, 0D6D, 04JC, 03EL, 03EK, 03D7, 06YU, 06YN. Blueprint main-20261015 def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback (order 1329) needs exactly this finite-level identification. The changed tower dependency is quoted correctly in step 6, and its strict-tower sentence adds no hypothesis. I accept the four tool_uses (K-flat resolution, derived change of rings, geometric inverse-image exactness, ringed compositors) as generic infrastructure. The DAG duplicate candidates are lem-pur-coefficient-pullback-comparison, which concerns extension rather than restriction, and lem-pur-independent-normalized-scalar-composition and the one-site tower node, which state less; none duplicates the item. One fault (E5), fixed: step 2 derived A/J_n'A ≅ u^{-1}(B/J_nB) from cokernel exactness 'by the same argument'. That needs u^{-1}(J_nB)=J_n'A. The step now gives the argument: u^{-1} preserves finite products, coproducts, epimorphisms and the monomorphism J_nB⊂B, so the sum-of-products epimorphism pulls back onto J_n'A. It also checks that the resulting isomorphism agrees with the map induced by A→B'→S_n', since R' surjects onto A/J_n'A.
